rule: A record identifies an exact missing arrow, proof step, source dependency, or typed obstruction boundary. It imposes no task on the user. Every logically dependent claim is downgraded, removed, or explicitly linked here.

statement: Siegel arXiv:2601.17030v3 Theorem 6.1 cannot presently support its printed periodic-point/rational-numen correspondence or its archimedean-divergence conclusion. The source sketch does not define the invoked canonical M_H(n), prove reverse-chronological branch correctness, establish local-to-global integrality, separate rational and zero fibres, or prove divergence in each asserted archimedean absolute value.
exact_missing_arrows: a typed canonical M_H(n) and retained digit-length coordinate
every reverse-chronological branch-membership implication for formal word fixed points
a proved passage from completion-level inverse integrality to global exact integrality
a valid theorem connecting full Minkowski escape to divergence at each claimed archimedean place
effect: CLM-COL-000041 remains a source-report record with status not_certified; neither direction is used downstream.
admission_boundary: A future correspondence statement must give explicit hypotheses and prove each displayed arrow. The already proved affine-word fixed-point theorem does not imply branch correctness or global integrality.

statement: Neither the nonarchimedean Fourier chain in arXiv:2601.17030v3 nor the targeted chi_3 inversion presentation in arXiv:2007.15936v3 is admitted at its printed scope. The former uses the wrong annihilator for the trace character unless the conductor is renormalized, omits trace adjoints for nonscalar branches, and retains support, finite-sum, zero-translation, index, and uniformizer-scaling defects. The latter misidentifies a dual group, has a reconstruction-sign error, and omits a subscript needed to type the finite characters.
exact_missing_arrows: the correct inverse-different frequency quotient or an explicitly renormalized character
the trace-adjoint frequency action for each nonscalar branch
an almost-sure support theorem sufficient for quotient descent
well-formed finite character sums with all variables and indices bound
the correct inversion sign and finite-character normalization in the chi_3 branch
effect: CLM-COL-000042 remains correction_required and no Fourier-decay or self-similar-measure consequence is used. The exact run-length/Haar/Syracuse coordinate theorem CLM-COL-000112 remains proved independently and does not depend on this record.
admission_boundary: Each versioned Fourier branch requires its own typed reconstruction. Equality of the underlying sample-space coordinate does not transfer either defective Fourier theorem.

statement: The raw Chatnotes coefficient passage does not construct a V-graded algebra of Collatz states or paths, a compatible color bracket, a degree-preserving bracket morphism to the Aizawa--Isaac--Segar algebras, or an action of those algebras on Collatz states or observables. The proved four-label evaluator and Fourier coefficient-algebra isomorphism do not supply those maps.

a bracket on homogeneous Collatz objects satisfying the color Jacobi identity
a typed degree-preserving bracket morphism to a cited color algebra or a proved representation on Collatz observables
an iteration-compatible composition law connecting affine branch words to the proposed algebra

a homomorphism between the relevant ambient group systems and a commutative comparison diagram relating the quotient map q:Spin(4) x SU(2)->(Spin(4) x SU(2))/<(-1,-1)> to the coefficient homomorphism partial:V->F_2 with Delta=ker(partial)

admission_boundary: Any future bridge must define its domain and codomain and prove grading, bracket, action, iteration, comparison-diagram, fibre, and inverse or obstruction statements. Shared degree labels or order-two data alone are insufficient.
